site.description: Software engineer, security architect and red teamer. I build considered software, question its assumptions and care about the details between.

hero.title: Care in the code.
hero.intro: I build considered software. Then question the assumptions holding it together.
hero.availability: Open to international roles, relocation & selected collaborations.

perspective.title: The small thing
perspective.text: A clear state. A deliberate boundary. A small feature that has been thought all the way through.
perspective.detail: That is where I like to work: connecting the architecture of a system to the experience of using it.

method.title: Understand first.
method.principle: Leaving it alone is better than changing it incorrectly.

steps.title: Trace the behavior.
steps.text: Follow the input, the rule and the result. Start with the system that exists.
steps.question: What is someone already depending on?

steps.title: Find the boundary.
steps.text: Look past the intended path. Make ownership, authority and failure states explicit.
steps.question: What still holds when the request is wrong?

steps.title: Protect the meaning.
steps.text: Make a focused change. Keep the evidence. Make the consequence clear in the interface.
steps.question: Can the difference be understood and reviewed?

about: I’m Parsa Emami, known online as parsaaemm. I follow software engineering and security together: how should a system work, and what happens when its assumptions are challenged?
Red teaming taught me to look beyond the intended path. Software engineering taught me that the response has to work for the application and the person using it.
I care about architecture, system design and the visual structure of software. I’m also studying Artificial Intelligence at master’s level.

projects.name: Attestara
projects.title: Keep the bytes, the policy and the signer separate.
projects.summary: A local release-evidence CLI that checks manifests, file bytes and SBOMs, evaluates the evidence-presence rule, and assesses signatures against independently configured trust.
projects.scope: The browser viewer inspects passport claims; verification runs in the Linux CLI.

projects.name: RiskWeft
projects.title: A security modeling direction, with its current scope in view.
projects.summary: A local-first web foundation with a roadmap browser and bounded JSON structure preview. The complete model-to-threat workflow is still being developed.
projects.scope: The current shell does not run the domain engine.

projects.name: MirageMesh
projects.title: A local security workflow, from sensor to incident.
projects.summary: A local-first security application with a supervised Go engine, isolated decoys, durable offline event spooling and a browser interface for incident replay and triage.
projects.scope: The reference workflow is verified on Ubuntu 24.04 Linux amd64. Other hosts require their own workflow evidence; the complete OSS v1 gate is pending.

experiment.title: One byte. Three different questions.
experiment.text: Change the sample, inspect its SHA-256 digest, sign it and choose whether to trust the demo key. Byte integrity, signature validity and key trust stay separate.
